Short answer: Your business should be the domain registrant and control the registrar login, recovery methods, and renewal. Give vendors limited access where the registrar allows it.

What this means for your business

The domain points customers, email, and search trust to the business. Losing control can interrupt more than the website. Verify the account before a launch, handoff, or dispute.

What to watch

  • The registrar account uses a vendor’s private email.
  • Renewal goes to an unknown card.
  • Two-factor authentication belongs to someone who left.
  • Nobody knows the registrar or has a current recovery route.

Do this next

  1. Use ICANN Lookup or your records to identify the registrar.
  2. Confirm the business can sign in and recover the account.
  3. Update authorized contacts and renewal payment carefully.
  4. Document DNS and email records before any transfer.

When Little Fight fits

We can map control, move access safely, and document the handoff. Ownership disputes may require the registrar, ICANN process, or legal advice.
